content:
maria: Quick q — thinking through DEK/KEK caching for private deployments. We hit KMS quota spikes in staging when many pods warmed DEKs at once. What's our recommended TTL and backoff?
jamal: rough rule: short-lived DEKs in memory for ~5-15m depending on QPS and blast radius. KEKs never cached raw, only reference tokens/ARNs.
alice: echo jamal. Also split hot vs cold keys: keep a small in-process cache for hot DEKs + a shared redis/LRU for warm ones. That reduces duplicate KMS unwraps.
maria: curious about security tradeoffs — if DEK cached 15m, revocation window is larger. How do we balance rotation/revoke vs latency?
oliver: revocation strategy: on rotation/revoke push an invalidation event to the keystore service + increment key version in metadata. Clients check version on request. For critical revoke, kill process token via node agent.
jamal: On KMS quotas: add jittered exponential backoff + local token-bucket per pod to smooth bursts. Also prefer async unwrap on request path with interim cached fallback if unwrap pending.
security-bot: FYI audit-log template: {actor, key_id, operation, wrap_type, result, trace_id, timestamp, region}. Include user_id and deployment_id for private installs.
alice: sample cache config (pseudocode):
```
cache: 
  local_ttl: 10m  # in-process
  shared_ttl: 60m  # redis LRU
  renew_threshold: 30s # start async refresh before expiry
  max_kms_retries: 5
  backoff: jittered_exponential(100ms, 3s)
```
maria: That helps — what about RBAC? Should decrypt permission be on service principal or on per-route identity?
oliver: We should use least privilege: service principal for keystore service (unwrap only), and short-lived credentials for apps limited to Get/Fetch metadata and call keystore service. That way KMS permissions are centralized.
jamal: For private deployments we also recommend using KMS external key references (no software KEK). When integrating with customer KMS, map customer's IAM to our keystore role for auditability.
sre-oncall: Incident playbook note: if KMS is throttling, fallback to read-only cached DEKs and degrade non-critical features. Alert thresholds: 5xx rate >1% AND kms_api_error_rate > 0.3 for 2m -> pager.
maria: vuln triage question: if a node is compromised, can attacker exfiltrate DEKs from in-process cache? Mitigations?
alice: yes risk exists. Mitigations: mlock key pages (when possible), restrict debug/syscalls, narrow process privileges, rotate affected DEKs, and if possible use HSM-backed KEKs where unwrap requires attestation.
jamal: add monitoring: frequent rekey events from a single instance -> suspicious. Also log unwrap source IP/instance-id in audit logs (redact token material).
security-bot: Action items: 1) Add recommended cache config to docs (maria) 2) Implement per-pod token-bucket backoff (eng-platform) 3) Update audit-log schema for private installs (security) 4) Draft incident runbook for KMS throttle (sre)
maria: I'll add the doc draft and link to a short TL;DR for customers with high-QPS patterns. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
